Pull over now, shut the engine off, and get everyone out and well away from the car. If you see any flames or smoke coming from under the hood, call 911 immediately — do NOT open the hood, as that feeds air to a fire and can make it much worse.

An engine-bay fire can escalate in under a minute, so treating this as urgent is the right call.

Once you're safely away from the car and it's cooled down, you'll need a mechanic to look at it before you drive it again. The burning-oil smell combined with heat can point to a few things — a leak hitting hot surfaces, degraded seals, worn gaskets — but none of them are safe to diagnose yourself or drive on. A BMW specialist should inspect the engine bay to confirm what's actually happening and whether it's safe to move the car to a shop.

Are you able to get it to a mechanic today, or do you need roadside help getting it to one?
